prompt:
(a) State what is meant by accuracy. [1]
(b) Explain what is meant by the true value of a physical quantity. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (a): The closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
Part (b): The value that would be obtained by an ideal measurement (or the accepted value from a trusted reference standard).

hints: In part (a), give the syllabus definition of accuracy.
In part (b), consider what value an ideal, error-free measurement would yield.
solution: (a) Accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity. (b) The true value is the value that would be obtained by an ideal measurement of the quantity.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Accuracy definition: the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
(b) True value: the ideal value of the quantity that an experimenter would measure if all experimental errors were eliminated.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored drill testing definitions of accuracy and true value.
